note: Configuration case, IP/MPLS L3VPN, device-config side. The same ACME L3VPN as the network model describes it, but in per-device routing-instance and BGP configuration. Carries the surface partners of the three traps (route-target near route-distinguisher; service-policy near routing-policy; bgp-neighbor near ce-neighbor) and one opaque vendor tag. ref=null marks an opaque item or native gap.

concepts.label: ip-vpn
concepts.gloss: the configured L3VPN identified across the devices by a common name and targets
concepts.example: vpn ACME configured on all three PEs

concepts.label: routing-instance
concepts.gloss: the per-device VRF holding the customer's routes on one router

concepts.label: attachment-circuit
concepts.gloss: the sub-interface binding a customer link into the VRF
concepts.example: ge-0/0/1.101 bound to vrf ACME on R-PE1

concepts.label: ce-device
concepts.gloss: the customer router reachable across the attachment circuit
concepts.example: the ACME headquarters router behind ge-0/0/1.101

concepts.label: rd
concepts.gloss: the route-distinguisher configured on a VRF to disambiguate its routes
concepts.example: rd 65000:101 under routing-instance ACME on R-PE1

concepts.label: route-target
concepts.gloss: the route-target community configured for import and export on a VRF
concepts.example: vrf-target import 65000:1 export 65000:1 on the hub VRF

concepts.label: interface-address
concepts.gloss: the IP address and mask configured on the attachment sub-interface

concepts.label: service-policy
concepts.gloss: the QoS policy-map attached to an attachment circuit to police and queue traffic

concepts.label: device
concepts.gloss: the physical PE router carrying the routing-instances

concepts.label: ce-protocol
concepts.gloss: the PE-CE routing protocol configured under the VRF for an attachment
concepts.example: bgp group CE-A under vrf ACME (eBGP to the customer)

concepts.label: route-map
concepts.gloss: the route-map filtering and setting attributes on VRF import and export

concepts.label: bgp-neighbor
concepts.gloss: the iBGP session to another PE that carries VPN routes in the provider core (device-config self-extension; no network-model counterpart)
concepts.example: neighbor 172.16.0.2 remote-as 65000 under the global BGP process
